n: A short lament that moves from despair to trust. “How long?” is asked four times in two verses. Will God forget David forever and hide his face?

f.w: How long wilt thou forget me

n: How long must David wrestle with his thoughts and carry sorrow every day while his enemy triumphs?

f.g: Agonize over plans in my mind.

n: Look at me and answer, Lord; brighten my eyes, or I will sleep the sleep of death.

f.g: Restore my strength and life — dim eyes were a sign of weakness.

n: Otherwise his enemy will say, “I beat him,” and his foes will celebrate when he stumbles.

f.g: When I am shaken or fall.

n: The turn: “But I have trusted in your steadfast love; my heart will rejoice in your salvation.” Nothing outward has changed — David has chosen trust.

f.w: I have trusted in thy mercy
f.g: “Mercy” is ḥesed — God’s faithful covenant love.

n: He will sing to the Lord, because God has been good to him.
